chapter: Brass bands, Eddie Miller and band stories
title: Eddie Miller and Ray Baduc
summary: Brownlee praises the professional dignity of Eddie Miller and Ray Baduc; the interviewer recalls first meeting Miller in a record shop.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Well, Eddie Miller, for instance, is a fine man. Ray Badouk. They all have been fine troopers and fine bandsmen. And one thing I could always admire about them, they always, uh, they were always dignified in their profession, in their business.

I would say Ray Badouk is, is outstanding in his carriage, and, uh, appearance, his, uh, loves a good time, but he knows where to break it off. He knows where to stop. Uh, I don't think at any time, as long as the many years that I've known Ray Badouk, I've never known him, to, uh, in any way, be out of command of himself, at all times, full command of his, his, uh, his being, himself. No matter where you meet him, he's always a fine boy, too. I'll never,

I'll never forget the first time I ever met Eddie Miller. I was working, uh, on Barone Street in a record shop with this man, two brothers, and, uh, Eddie comes in, he's got on a Hollywood silk sports shirt, and, uh, real fine slacks, you know? Yeah. And all that, you know, just, uh, sporty, but obviously all of this was just in perfect taste.
I see. And, uh, yes, that was it.
And it just reeked of money, you know?

Little, little prince. He's a little prince. I've always, I, I could just call him the little prince. I think that he, uh, Eddie's fine, and he, he's always liked and everybody ever, in recording sessions, everybody's always wanted him. Mm-hmm.
When he left the shop, though, this, the other fellow up there in the shop looks over and says, who was that?
well, that was Eddie Miller. He said,
he doesn't look like a musician. You know?
Well, there's a lot of them that don't look like them, but they're very fine. Yeah, well,

uh, I think, uh, one of my favorite clarinet players never bothers to dress up, you know? I think, uh, one, one guy like that around the wall, and she just doesn't, doesn't care unless he's got a job, I don't know. And, uh, so many of them like that. But, uh, we're getting off the subject and everything.
